milestone.title: Bulk milestone operations — multi-target metadata writes without agent loops

intent.outcome: Agents change milestone metadata (priority, depends_on, spec_status, execution block/defer) across many milestones in one mp command — using --ids or the same --where filters as list milestones — instead of shell for-loops over mp milestone set-priority / update. mp runs writes sequentially, returns per-id results { succeeded, failed, results[] }, and supports --dry-run. Complements M79/M88 bulk review ops and M93 single-milestone fragment ops; closes the remaining agent loop pattern for plan metadata.

problem.description: M79 and M88 eliminated jq loops and bulk review/finding writes, but milestone-level metadata still requires one subprocess per id. Observed agent pattern: for id in 82 92 93; do mp milestone set-priority $id high; done — and similar loops to add the same depends_on entry or set spec_status=review on every milestone matching a filter. Each iteration re-pays CLI startup, loses atomic reporting (which id failed?), and pushes orchestration to the shell. list milestones already supports --where and --include for bulk reads; reviews pass supports --all. Milestone writes have no symmetric bulk API. M93 deliberately scopes to single-milestone fragment ops (ac/step/wp). Cross-milestone scalar metadata updates need a first-class bulk layer.

in_scope: Target resolution: --ids and --where are unioned (dedupe); error if both empty
Response shape: { ok, dry_run, target_count, succeeded, failed, results: [{ id, ok, error? }] }
Sequential execution; continue on per-id failure; exit non-zero if any failed (unless --keep-going documents otherwise)
Integration tests: ids list, where filter, dry-run, partial failure, depends_on add/remove
Document in AGENTS.md, AGENT-READINESS, MP-COMMANDS — anti-pattern: shell for-loop over set-priority/update
out_of_scope: Bulk fragment ops (ac/step/wp) — M93 single-milestone only
Bulk milestone complete, bulk reviews pass — reviews pass --all exists
Bulk array replacement on milestone update — M93 --replace-arrays migration escape hatch only
Transactional all-or-nothing batch (partial success is a feature)

findings.description: Bulk set-spec-status bypasses G2/G3/G4/G14 gates that single-id enforces. Reproducer: bulk set-spec-status --ids M01 --status review succeeds on a milestone with no acceptance_criteria, even though single-id set-spec-status correctly rejects with G3. AC-02 specifies per-id results with errors but doesn't mention gate parity — the gap is that bulk ignores the validation surface entirely. Fix: call gate_errors_for_spec_status + check_g14_approval_requests per id, surface errors as per-id rows, let other ids still process.
findings.author: pi-coding-agent

findings.description: Dry-run on depends-on add silently marks would-fail rows as ok. Reproducer: A->[]  and  B->[A]; bulk depends-on add --ids A --depends-on B --dry-run returns ok:true for A, but the live run correctly identifies the A->B->A cycle. Dry-run should preview cycle failures per id, not lie about success. Fix: run cycle detection in dry-run mode too; report per-id ok:false with the cycle error when the would-be add is cyclic.
findings.author: pi-coding-agent

findings.description: Operation-level args (priority, status, depends_on target existence) are not validated up-front. Result: --priority critical reports the same error N times for N targets; --depends-on M9999 runs cycle detection against a non-existent node N times. Fix: validate priority/spec_status against the static enum at dispatch time, and resolve --depends-on existence once per batch (not per id).
findings.author: pi-coding-agent

findings.description: Dead code: result_row_for_tests helper is unused (marked #[allow(dead_code)]); result_row is the only caller and it's already exercised via result_row itself. Just remove the wrapper.
findings.author: pi-coding-agent

findings.description: depends_on_creates_cycle loads all milestones from disk on every per-id add (N loads for batch of N). For projects with thousands of milestones this is wasteful. Fix: load the graph once at the start of run_bulk and thread it through; for set-priority/set-spec-status, drop the per-id peek (the before/after can use the milestone already in scope, or skip before when it would require an extra load).
findings.author: pi-coding-agent

findings.description: F-06: When load_milestone_by_id fails for a target id (e.g. bogus --ids M9999), the row reports "before": null. Since the milestone couldn't be loaded, "before" should be omitted (None) rather than emitted as JSON null — null looks like a legitimate (missing) value. Fix: in apply_set_priority / apply_set_spec_status / apply_add_depends_on / apply_remove_depends_on, treat load failure as before=None and let the per-id error explain.
findings.author: pi-coding-agent

findings.description: F-07: F-03 over-corrected — bulk depends-on remove now rejects --depends-on <id> when that id is not a milestone in the plan. Reproducer: mp milestone bulk depends-on remove --ids 01 --depends-on 99 errors with "depends_on target 99 does not match any milestone in the plan" even though remove is naturally a no-op for a non-existent dep. The spec doesn't require the dep target to exist for remove. Fix: only enforce the existence check for depends-on add (where the target becomes a real edge); for remove, accept any --depends-on value and let the no-op semantics apply. Keeps the cycle/existence guard for the meaningful case.
findings.author: pi-coding-agent

findings.description: F-08: --where '' (empty string) silently matches all milestones in both bulk and list. Reproducer: mp list milestones --where '' returns every milestone; bulk --where '' matches all. Root cause: parse_where_filters skips empty entries; empty filter list vacuously satisfies .all(); no guard. Pre-existing in list, propagated by bulk. Fix: when --where has any non-empty entry that didn't parse, bail (already done); additionally bail when --where is present but entirely empty/blank so the user gets a clear error instead of a silent all-match. Inherit the fix into list milestones for parity.
findings.author: pi-coding-agent

findings.description: F-09: Awkward empty-branch code in dry-run path of run_bulk — . The empty if branch is dead. Refactor to a single  after dropping the empty branch.
findings.author: pi-coding-agent

findings.description: F-10: TOCTOU on cycle pre-check. depends_on_creates_cycle_in_graph uses the graph loaded at dispatch time. If another process modifies deps between graph load and our write, the pre-check can false-positive (cycle reported but live would succeed) or false-negative (cycle not detected). For single-agent CLI use this is acceptable, but worth documenting as a known concurrency caveat in the docstring or docs. Could add a lockfile later if multi-process becomes a real workflow.
findings.author: pi-coding-agent
